title: A fixed early 36.501-day wave reduces 2014 GJ 674 velocity error by 47 percent, but block ranges include zero
abstract: We search 58 public GJ 674 HARPS velocities from 2013 for a residual sine wave after terms for the known planet. The strongest early period is 36.501 days. Its fixed early coefficients reduce weighted squared error by 46.8 percent in 67 velocities from 2014. A conditional 30-day resampling range is -36.9 to +59.6 percent. Two other reductions give gains of 44.6 and 48.8 percent, with ranges that include zero. Early null tests depend strongly on block length. H-alpha and line width also vary at the selected period. These results permit a rotation-related explanation but do not prove a cause or establish a new planet. The products share HARPS spectra. No independent instrument confirms a new signal. Signal recovery is limited. Code, raw input, hashes, controls, figure, and offline steps are included.

display.caption: The early search selects 36.501 days. The fixed early wave reduces later point error in three products. The 30-day ranges include zero. Both seasons are resampled at the fixed selected frequency.
